author: David Leisering
title: Gabriel Moreno hits go-ahead homer in eighth inning Sunday
desc: Gabriel Moreno had only one hit in five at bats on Sunday, but his hit was a go-ahead solo home run in the eighth inning to lift the Diamondbacks to a 5-3 win over the Reds.
impact: Moreno snapped a 3-3 tie as he took Zach Maxwell deep in the eighth inning for his sixth home run of the season. The catcher got off to a slow start but is heating up as of late, batting .346 (9-for-26) with three home runs over his last seven games. For the year, Moreno is batting .264 with six home runs, 23 RBI, and four steals in 47 games. He hit a career-high nine home runs last season and posted career-highs in RBI (50) and steals (6) in 2023. Moreno appears poised to take a run at all three of those numbers in 2026.

author: David Leisering
title: Tommy Troy goes deep in Sunday victory over Reds
desc: Tommy Troy went 1-for-3 with a solo home run on Sunday in a 5-3 victory over the Reds.
impact: Troy connected for his second home run of the season off of Cincinnati starter, Andrew Abbott, to get Arizona on the board in the third inning. Troy started his big league career on a four-game hitting streak during which he hit .417 (5-for-12). However, since then, the rookie has hit just .178 (8-for-45) with 12 strikeouts over his last 15 games. It's been even worse in his last seven outings as he is in the midst of a 2-for-21 skid at the dish. Overall, Troy is hitting .228 with a .691 OPS in his first 19 big league games.

author: David Leisering
title: Geraldo Perdomo homers, steals base in Sunday victory
desc: Geraldo Perdomo went 2-for-3 with a two-run homer, a walk, and a stolen base on Sunday, helping the Diamondbacks to a 5-3 over the Reds.
impact: Perdomo hit his two-run homer off of Tejay Antone with one out in the sixth inning, giving Arizona a 3-2 lead at the time. Earlier in the game, he reached on a bunt single and later, he walked and stole second. The home run was just his fourth of the year and his first since May 29 in Seattle. Meanwhile, the stolen base was his 11th in 16 tries this season. Perdomo is hitting .348 (8-for-23) with a homer and three steals over his last seven games and is batting .333 (14-for-42) in 13 contests this month.

author: David Leisering
title: Paul Sewald slams door on Reds for 17th save of season
desc: Paul Sewald pitched a scoreless ninth inning for his 17th save of the season on Sunday as the Diamondbacks held on for a 5-3 win in Cincinnati.
impact: Sewald walked Matt McLain to start the ninth, but then retired the next three batters - including a strikeout of Will Benson - to earn his 17th save in 18 chances this season. The righthander has not allowed a run in his last six outings (six innings) and has given up only one run in his last 11 appearances (11 innings). Overall, Sewald is 2-4 with a 3.08 ERA in 29 appearances and has allowed only 12 hits with a 29:7 K:BB ratio over 26.1 innings.

author: David Leisering
title: Zac Gallen goes six innings in no-decision Sunday
desc: Zac Gallen allowed three runs on six hits, walked two, and struck out four in a no-decision on Sunday.
impact: Gallen has now allowed at least three earned runs in five consecutive outings and in eight of his last nine starts. The righthander also served up two more home runs on Sunday and has allowed 11 homers over his last nine outings. Gallen pitched to a 7.04 ERA in six May starts and is now 0-1 with a 6.06 ERA in three June appearances. Overall, Gallen is 3-5 with a 5.35 ERA in 15 starts this season and has struck out only 50 batters in 75.2 innings. He's scheduled to take on the Twins at home on Saturday in his next start.

author: David Leisering
title: Donovan Walton hits first home run of season Sunday
desc: Donovan Walton went 1-for-3 with a solo home run on Sunday in the Angels' 8-3 loss to the Rays.
impact: Walton connected on a pitch from Ian Seymour in the fifth inning for his first home run of the year and his first since September 15, 2024 as a member of the Giants. It was only his fifth career home run in 90 games at the big league level. In limited action this season, Walton is hitting .296 (16-for-54) with a home run and four RBI in 18 games.

author: David Leisering
title: Colin Rea suffers loss in bulk relief role Sunday
desc: Colin Rea suffered the loss on Sunday after he allowed four runs on six hits, walked three, and struck out two over 4.2 innings in a bulk relief outing.
impact: Rea followed Ryan Rolison, who served as the Cubs' opener and who needed only 11 pitches to retire all four batters he faced. Rea did not fare as well as he was charged with the loss after allowing four runs and ten baserunners (six hits, three walks, one hit batter). The righthander has struggled of late, going 0-2 with a 7.98 ERA and a 7:8 K:BB ratio in three appearances this month. With Matthew Boyd (knee) scheduled to resume throwing this week, Rea looks like he may be the odd man out of the rotation after Boyd returns - unless he can turn things around soon.

author: David Leisering
title: Ryan Rolison retires all four batters he faces as opener Sunday
desc: Ryan Rolison served as an opener for the first time this season on Sunday and retired all four batters he faced in the Cubs' 5-1 loss to the Giants.
impact: Rolison made his first start of the season and second of his career on Sunday and needed just 11 pitches to get four outs. The lefthander has not allowed an earned run in his last 10 appearances covering a span of 13 innings. In that stretch, Rolison has allowed only six hits and has an 11:6 K:BB ratio. After posting a 7.02 ERA in 31 appearances as a rookie last season, Rolison is 5-1 with a 2.13 ERA in 21 outings this season. It's unknown if he will continue to serve as an opener moving forward or if he will move back to the middle innings of the Cubs' bullpen.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Ben Williamson blasts one over fence Sunday
desc: Ben Williamson went 1-for-4 with a solo home run in Sunday's 8-3 win over the Los Angeles Angels.
impact: After 50 games, Williamson finally connected for his first home run of the 2026 season. Given his career .319 slugging percentage, fantasy managers should not expect home runs to become a regular part of his production. Despite going deep on Sunday, he has struggled overall in June, slashing .200/.250/.333 across 30 at-bats.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Junior Caminero connects for homer Sunday
desc: Junior Caminero went 1-for-5 with a home run, two RBI and a run scored in Sunday's 8-3 win over the Los Angeles Angels.
impact: Caminero launched a 374-foot homer off Sam Bachman in the eighth inning, snapping a home run drought that dated back to June 1. He has now reached base safely in six consecutive games and is slashing .239/.340/.435 across 46 at-bats in June.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Victor Mesa Jr. goes deep Sunday
desc: Victor Mesa Jr. went 2-for-3 with a home run, a walk, two runs scored and two RBI in Sunday's 8-3 win over the Los Angeles Angels.
impact: Mesa recorded his first hit since June 7 on Sunday and made it count, launching a 406-foot home run to right-center field off Sam Bachman in the eighth inning. Despite the long ball, Mesa is hitting just .200 with a .669 OPS on the season and remains best left on waivers.

author: David Leisering
title: Pete Crow-Armstrong stays hot in loss to Giants on Sunday
desc: Pete Crow-Armstrong went 2-for-4 with a pair of singles and a stolen base on Sunday during the Cubs' 5-1 loss to the Giants.
impact: Crow-Armstrong is one of the hottest hitters in the game right now as he has now hit safely in 17 of his last 18 games and is batting .377 (29-for-77) during that stretch. He's up to .392 (20-for-51) with five home runs and four steals in 12 games this month. His stolen base on Sunday was his 16th of the season - fifth-most in the National League. Crow-Armstrong has also improved his plate discipline this season, having already drawn 24 walks in just 72 games. He had a career-high 29 walks in 157 games a year ago.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Cedric Mullins II swipes bag Sunday
desc: Cedric Mullins II went 2-for-3 with a walk, one run scored and two stolen bases in Sunday's 8-3 win over the Los Angeles Angels.
impact: Mullins recorded his second consecutive multi-hit game on Sunday and added two stolen bases in the process. He's been excellent in June, slashing .281/.425/.563 with three home runs and two steals. After a slow start to the season, Mullins has turned things around in June and is worth considering in deeper fantasy leagues, especially given the power and speed combination he's providing.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Joe Mack goes yard Sunday
desc: Joe Mack went 1-for-4 with a home run, one walk, one run scored and an RBI in Sunday's 4-2 victory over the Pittsburgh Pirates.
impact: After going hitless in the first two games of the series, Mack bounced back in a big way on Sunday by launching a 424-foot solo home run off Paul Skenes in the sixth inning. Mack has been swinging a hot bat in June, slashing .313/.371/.531 across 32 at-bats.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Heriberto Hernandez launches homer Sunday
desc: Heriberto Hernandez went 1-for-4 with a solo home run in Sunday's 4-2 victory over the Pittsburgh Pirates.
impact: Hernandez took Paul Skenes deep in the second inning with a 404-foot blast to left-center field. He started all three games during the weekend series, going 4-for-12 with a home run, a double, one walk, two runs scored and three RBI. Hernandez is now slashing .333/.368/.694 across 36 at-bats in June and is emerging as a viable option in deeper fantasy leagues thanks to his consistent playing time and hot bat.
